summary: Google lets you build and test an OAuth app on your own quickly. To let strangers connect their Gmail, Google reviews your app first, and how long that takes depends on how sensitive your requested permissions (scopes) are. The heaviest path adds an outside security assessment.

verdict.headline: Easy to start in testing mode, but real users need Google's verification: about two weeks for sensitive scopes, about six weeks plus a third-party security assessment for restricted ones.

wait.label: About 10 business days (sensitive) to about 6 weeks (restricted)

prerequisites.item: A public home page and privacy policy on the same domain
prerequisites.detail: The privacy policy must be linked from your OAuth consent screen, and the domain verified in Google Search Console.

prerequisites.item: A written reason for every sensitive scope
prerequisites.detail: Explain what each scope does for users and why a narrower scope would not work.

prerequisites.item: An unlisted YouTube demo video, in English
prerequisites.detail: It shows the consent flow, your app name, the OAuth client ID in the address bar, and how each sensitive or restricted scope is used.

prerequisites.item: Current project owner and editor contacts
prerequisites.detail: Google's review team emails these accounts, and unanswered emails can pause the review.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and an OAuth client
steps.detail: This is the starting point for any Google API. The pages read for this guide cover verification, not project setup, so follow Google's console prompts.

steps.title: Request only the scopes you need
steps.detail: Add scopes on the Data Access page. The console labels each one non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted. Asking for more than a feature needs violates Google's minimum-scope policy.

steps.title: Build and test in Testing status
steps.detail: Projects kept in Testing are exempt from verification. If you launch unverified with sensitive or restricted scopes, you are capped at 100 new users for the life of the project.

steps.title: Publish the public pages and verify your domain
steps.detail: Home page, privacy policy on the same domain, and domain ownership in Search Console.

steps.title: Write scope justifications and record the demo video
steps.detail: The agent drafts the text and the video script. You record and upload the unlisted video.

steps.title: Verify and publish your branding
steps.detail: Branding checks are usually quick. A passing result expires after 7 days if you do not publish it, and you need published branding before the data access review.

steps.title: Request the data access review
steps.detail: Submit in the Verification Center and answer any follow-up from Google's Trust and Safety team.

steps.title: If you have restricted scopes, complete the security assessment
steps.detail: A Google-approved independent assessor checks your app against the CASA framework when restricted data passes through or is stored on a server you run. Plan to repeat it every year.

limits.title: 100-user cap while unverified
limits.detail: Counts new users across the whole project lifetime and cannot be reset. Check usage under APIs and Services, OAuth Consent Screen.

limits.title: Branding results expire in 7 days
limits.detail: Publish promptly after Verify Branding passes.

limits.title: Yearly re-verification for restricted scopes
limits.detail: Reverification and reassessment at least every 12 months, and adding a new restricted scope may trigger it.

limits.title: Data handling rules
limits.detail: Restricted-scope apps follow the Google API Services User Data Policy, including Limited Use, and must delete user data on request.

blockers.problem: Review paused by a follow-up email
blockers.why: Google's Trust and Safety team may ask questions, and the review waits for your answer.
blockers.nextMove: Keep owner and editor contacts current, and have the agent draft replies for you to approve.

blockers.problem: You hit the 100-user cap before verification finishes
blockers.why: Unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes stop letting new users sign in at the cap.
blockers.nextMove: Start verification before you invite users, and watch cap usage on the consent screen page.

blockers.problem: A restricted scope triggers a security assessment
blockers.why: It needs an outside assessor and repeats yearly. The pages read do not state its cost.
blockers.nextMove: Check whether a narrower scope covers your feature before you commit to the restricted one.

blockers.why: Google reads a broad scope used for a narrow job as a policy violation.
blockers.nextMove: Ask for the narrowest scope that does the job, and explain in the justification why nothing narrower works.

agentCanDo: Map your features to the narrowest Gmail scopes and flag likely classifications to confirm in the console
Draft the privacy policy, home page copy and per-scope justifications
Write the demo video script and a pre-submission checklist
Track review status and draft replies to Google's follow-up emails
Create the Composio auth config once you have a client ID and secret
youMustDo: Sign in to Google Cloud and Search Console, and prove domain ownership with DNS
Record and upload the unlisted demo video
Submit branding and the data access review from the project owner account
Commission the CASA security assessment if restricted scopes apply

uncertainties: The pages read do not say which Gmail scopes are sensitive or restricted. The Cloud Console labels each scope when you add it, so confirm there.
The cost of the CASA security assessment is not stated on the pages read.
The sensitive-scope page says up to 10 days; the FAQ says about 10 business days. This guide uses the longer reading: about two weeks of calendar time.
Google calls the timelines estimates, not guarantees, and says they vary with how quickly you respond.
Setting up the Cloud project and OAuth client is not covered by the pages read.

corrections.was: The Google help-center overview page looks like the whole verification process.
corrections.now: Steps, the 100-user cap, timelines and the security assessment are on four separate Google pages.
